styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small shelf cabinet with a brown wood frame and cream candles on shelves. Per-tile density is fine: median 14 colours per tile, above the hedge (10) and near the stall (17) and well (20). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no flat areas. Against that, only 15 distinct colours are spread over wood, shelf interior and candles. That is about 4 wood steps, fewer than the 5-6 on the stall and well, and it matches only the thinner references (bench 14, lamp 14, hedge 11). 68% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, higher than the bench (44%), the stall (1%) and the well (33%). So the outline leans toward a dark sticker line, with some brown tint on the frame, rather than the material-toned edges of the richer references. Texture is limited to shelf and candle detail with little wood grain. It is clean and readable but slightly shallower and more outline-driven than the better Beodeul pieces. Since this is a borderline call, it fails.

Measured facts support it: 14 colours per 16x16 tile (references 10-20 where measurable), 0% flat-fill coverage, and 15 distinct colours, in line with the bench and lamp (14 each) though well below the stall and well (38-40).
